{"self_assessment": "Impact: I contributed to the top line of our fish, laying about a dozen dominoes by tracing stroke 1 on from the line near the tail loop. I also stood one fallen domino back up. The fish was recognizable and nearly all of it connects to the start, so my pieces sit in a working picture. My part was modest next to the whole build, and I'd rather say that plainly than inflate it.

Execution: I inspected the tail fork and the belly early on and reported that I saw no gaps. I checked the build again at several points later (around 5:00, 5:15, 5:45 and 6:15) to make sure the connections held. When we ran short of dominoes, I kept my hands off, so I didn't use up supply or risk bumping neighbors' work. I stayed off the start domino and the tail, as agreed.

Collaboration: I asked early whether the tail was its own stroke, so I understood the design before building. I offered to take over the top line and waited for Hana's go-ahead before laying anything, so we never doubled up. I kept my updates short and clear, and I acknowledged Sofia, Omar and Hana's work during the closing stretch. In the last two minutes I helped keep the table calm and hands-off.

Leadership: I took ownership of a piece of work, the top line toward the nose, and started on it as soon as I was cleared to. I followed the table's plan, respected the hands-off agreement before the push, and encouraged the team in the final stretch. I didn't try to override the plan once the top line was handed on. I'd like to take on more of the central stretches next time and build them with more pace.", "my_share_percent": 10}
